title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第二十一: 魏徵 Volume 71 Biographies 21: Wei Zheng

sentences.zh: 魏徵

translations.literal: Wei Zheng
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng

sentences.zh: 魏徵，字玄成，鉅鹿曲城人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng, courtesy name Xuancheng, was a native of Qucheng in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng, courtesy name Xuancheng, came from Qucheng in Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父長賢，北齊屯留令。

translations.literal: His father Changxian was Magistrate of Tunliu under Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei Changxian had been magistrate of Tunliu under the Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 徵少孤貧，落拓有大志，不事生業，出家爲道士。

translations.literal: In youth Zheng was orphaned and poor, unrestrained and possessed of great ambition; he did not engage in livelihood pursuits and left home to become a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he was free-spirited and ambitious, took no regular livelihood, and became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，多所通涉，見天下漸亂，尤屬意縱橫之説。

translations.literal: He loved reading and was broadly learned; seeing the realm falling into disorder, he especially devoted himself to the arts of vertical and horizontal alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, and as the realm slid into chaos he especially studied the arts of alliance and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 大業末，武陽郡丞元寶藏舉兵以應李密，召徵使典書記。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, Yuan Baocang, Assistant Magistrate of Wuyang commandery, raised troops in response to Li Mi and summoned Zheng to serve as recorder of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign, Yuan Baocang, assistant magistrate of Wuyang, raised forces for Li Mi and summoned Zheng to keep his records.

sentences.zh: 密毎見寶藏之疎，未嘗不稱善，既聞徵所爲，遽使召之。

translations.literal: Whenever Mi saw Baocang's memorials he always praised them; on hearing what Zheng had written, he immediately sent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi always praised Baocang's memorials; when he heard what Zheng had written, he sent for him at once.

sentences.zh: 徵進十策以干密，雖奇之而不能用。

translations.literal: Zheng presented ten stratagems to gain Mi's attention; though Mi admired them, he could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng offered ten policy proposals to Li Mi; though Mi admired them, he did not put them into practice.

sentences.zh: 及王世充攻密於洛口，徵説密長史鄭頲曰：「魏公雖驟勝，而驍將銳卒死傷多矣；

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong attacked Mi at Luokou, Zheng said to Mi's Chief Clerk Zheng Ting, "Though the Duke of Wei has won swift victories, many brave generals and sharp soldiers have been killed or wounded;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong attacked Li Mi at Luokou, Zheng said to Li Mi's chief clerk Zheng Ting, "The Duke of Wei has won quick victories, but many of his best generals and troops are dead or wounded;

sentences.zh: 又軍無府庫，有功不賞。

translations.literal: moreover the army has no granaries, and achievements go unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: moreover the army has no stores, and merit goes unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 戰士心惰，此二者難以應敵。

translations.literal: The soldiers' hearts are slack — these two conditions make it hard to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: the men's spirits are flagging — with these two problems, it will be hard to face the enemy.

sentences.zh: 未若深溝高壘，曠日持久，不過旬月，敵人糧盡，可不戰而退，追而擊之，取勝之道。

translations.literal: It would be better to dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts, protract the time day after day, and within no more than a month or two the enemy's grain will be exhausted; then they can withdraw without fighting, and you can pursue and strike them — that is the way to victory.
translations.idiomatic: Better to dig deep trenches, raise high walls, and wear them down: within a month or two their supplies will fail, they will retreat without a battle, and you can pursue and defeat them — that is the path to victory.

sentences.zh: 且東都食盡，世充計窮，意欲死戰，可謂窮寇難與爭鋒，請慎無與戰。」

translations.literal: Moreover the eastern capital's food is exhausted, Shichong's plans are at an end, and he intends to fight to the death — one may say a cornered foe is hard to contend with blade to blade; please be careful not to give battle."
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital is starving, Shichong is at his wit's end, and he means to fight to the death — a desperate enemy is hard to meet blade to blade. Please do not give battle."

sentences.zh: 頲曰：「此老生之常談耳！」

translations.literal: Zheng Ting said, "This is the old man's shopworn talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ting said, "This is the old man's shopworn talk!"

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「此乃奇謀深策，何謂常談？」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "This is an ingenious stratagem and deep counsel — why call it shopworn talk?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "This is ingenious and far-sighted counsel — why call it shopworn talk?"

sentences.zh: 因拂衣而去。

translations.literal: With that he shook out his robes and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he shook out his robes and left.

sentences.zh: 及密敗，徵隨密來降，至京師，久不見知。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, Zheng followed Mi in surrendering; arriving at the capital, he long went unrecognized.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's defeat Zheng surrendered with him to the capital, where for a long time he received no notice.

sentences.zh: 自請安輯山東，乃授秘書丞，驅傳至黎陽。

translations.literal: He himself requested to pacify Shandong, and was then appointed Secretary Director and sent by fast relay to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to pacify the east, was appointed secretary director, and was sent by fast relay to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 時徐世勣尚爲李密擁眾，徵與世勣書曰：

translations.literal: At that time Xu Shiji still held troops for Li Mi; Zheng wrote to Shiji, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji still held Li Mi's forces; Zheng wrote to him as follows:

sentences.zh: 自隋末亂離，群雄競逐，跨州連郡，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Since the disorder and separation at the end of Sui, heroes have raced to seize power, spanning provinces and linking commanderies beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos at the end of Sui, rival leaders have seized territory across provinces and commanderies beyond count.

sentences.zh: 魏公起自叛徒，奮臂大呼，四方響應，萬里風馳，雲合霧聚，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei rose from among rebels, threw up his arms and cried out, and the four quarters answered; like wind over ten thousand li, clouds gathered and mist massed — his followers numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei rose from rebellion, raised his banner, and drew responses from every quarter; hosts in the hundreds of thousands gathered to him like wind and storm.

sentences.zh: 威之所被，將半天下，破世充於洛口，摧化及於黎山。

translations.literal: Where his authority reached, nearly half the realm was his; he broke Shichong at Luokou and crushed Huaji at Lishan.
translations.idiomatic: His power covered nearly half the realm; he broke Wang Shichong at Luokou and crushed Yu Huaji at Lishan.

sentences.zh: 方欲西蹈咸陽，北凌玄闕，揚旌瀚海，飲馬渭川，翻以百勝之威，敗於奔亡之虜。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to march west upon Xianyang and north to threaten the capital, to raise banners on the Hanhai and water horses at the Wei River, he turned the prestige of a hundred victories into defeat at the hands of fleeing remnants.
translations.idiomatic: He was poised to march on Xianyang, threaten the capital, and carry his banners to the northern seas — yet the prestige of a hundred victories collapsed before a broken foe in flight.

sentences.zh: 固知神器之重，自有所歸，不可以力爭。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the weight of the Mandate belongs where it belongs and cannot be seized by force alone.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the Mandate has its rightful holder and cannot be taken by force alone.

sentences.zh: 是以魏公思皇天之乃睠，入函谷而不疑。

translations.literal: Therefore the Duke of Wei, mindful of Heaven's favor, entered Hangu Pass without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: So the Duke of Wei, trusting Heaven's favor, entered Hangu Pass without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 公生於擾攘之時，感知己之遇。

translations.literal: You were born in turbulent times and felt the debt owed a patron who recognized your worth.
translations.idiomatic: You came of age in turmoil and owed your patron a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 根本已拔，確乎不動，鳩合遺散，據守一隅。

translations.literal: Though the root was already uprooted, you stood firm and unmoved, gathered the scattered remnants, and held a corner of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Though the main force was gone, you held your ground, rallied the scattered, and kept a foothold.

sentences.zh: 世充以乘勝餘勇，息其東略；

translations.literal: Shichong, riding the momentum of victory, paused his eastern advance;
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, flush with victory, halted his advance to the east;

sentences.zh: 建德因侮亡之勢，不敢南謀。

translations.literal: Jiande, taking advantage of a fallen foe's weakness, did not dare plan southward.
translations.idiomatic: and Dou Jiande, seeing a beaten enemy, did not dare move south.

sentences.zh: 公之英聲，足以振於今古。

translations.literal: Your noble reputation is enough to resound through past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Your reputation already resounds through past and present.

sentences.zh: 然誰無善始，終之慮難。

translations.literal: Yet who does not begin well? The worry is how one ends.
translations.idiomatic: Who does not begin well? The hard part is the end.

sentences.zh: 去就之機，安危大節。

translations.literal: The moment of going or staying is a great matter of safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: The choice of allegiance is a matter of life and death.

sentences.zh: 若策名得地，則九族廕其餘輝；

translations.literal: If you attach your name to the right lord and gain a place, then nine clans will share the afterglow;
translations.idiomatic: Attach yourself to the right lord and your whole clan will share the reward;

sentences.zh: 委質非人，則一身不能自保。

translations.literal: if you offer your service to the wrong man, then even your own person cannot be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: serve the wrong master and not even your own life will be secure.

sentences.zh: 殷鑑不遠，公所聞見。

translations.literal: The mirror of Yin is not far off — you have seen and heard it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Recent examples are close at hand — you have seen them yourself.

sentences.zh: 孟賁猶豫，童子先之，知幾其神，不俟終日。

translations.literal: Meng Ben hesitated, and a child went ahead of him; to know the moment is divine — one should not wait even a day.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ben hesitated while a child went first; to read the moment is wisdom — do not wait even a day.

sentences.zh: 今公處必爭之地，乘宜速之機，更事遲疑，坐觀成敗，恐凶狡之輩，先人生心，則公之事去矣。

translations.literal: Now you stand on ground that must be contested and ride a moment that calls for speed; if you delay and watch outcomes from the sidelines, I fear the vicious and cunning will get there first — then your cause will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: You stand on contested ground at a moment that demands speed; if you hesitate and watch from the sidelines, the ruthless will move first — and your cause will be lost.

sentences.zh: 世勣得書，遂定計遣使歸國，開倉運糧，以饋淮安王神通之軍。

translations.literal: Shiji received the letter, settled on a plan, sent envoys to submit to the state, opened the granaries, and transported grain to supply the army of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji received the letter, submitted to the Tang, opened the granaries, and sent grain to Prince Huai'an Li Shentong's army.

sentences.zh: 俄而建德悉眾南下，攻陷黎陽，獲徵，署爲起居舍人。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiande marched south with his full force, captured Liyang, seized Zheng, and appointed him Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dou Jiande marched south in force, took Liyang, captured Zheng, and made him drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 及建德就擒，與裴矩西入關。

translations.literal: When Jiande was captured, Zheng entered the Pass westward with Pei Ju.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande was taken, Zheng entered the Pass with Pei Ju.

sentences.zh: 隱太子聞其名，引直洗馬，甚禮之。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince heard his name and summoned him as Direct Attendant of the Heir Apparent, treating him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden crown prince Li Jiancheng heard of him, made him direct attendant in the Eastern Palace, and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 徵見太宗勳業日隆，毎勸建成早爲之所。

translations.literal: Zheng saw that Taizong's achievements grew daily and repeatedly urged Jiancheng to act against him early.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Taizong's power grow daily, Zheng repeatedly urged Jiancheng to move against him early.

sentences.zh: 及敗，太宗使召之，謂曰：「汝離間我兄弟，何也？」

translations.literal: After the defeat, Taizong sent to summon him and said to him, "You drove a wedge between my brothers — why?"
translations.idiomatic: After the Xuanwu Gate coup Taizong sent for him and said, "You set my brothers against each other — why?"

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「皇太子若從徵言，必無今日之禍。」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Had the crown prince followed my words, he would never have met today's disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Had the crown prince heeded me, he would not have met today's disaster."

sentences.zh: 太宗素器之，引爲詹事主簿。

translations.literal: Taizong had long admired his talent and appointed him Chief Clerk in the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had long valued his ability and made him chief clerk in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，擢拜諫議大夫，封鉅鹿縣男，使安輯河北，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he promoted Zheng to Remonstrance and Policy Advisor, enfeoffed him as Baron of Julu, sent him to pacify Hebei, and authorized him to act as expedient circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On taking the throne he made Zheng remonstrance and policy advisor, enfeoffed him as Baron of Julu, sent him to pacify Hebei, and authorized discretionary action.

sentences.zh: 徵至磁州，遇前宮千牛李志安、齊王護軍李思行錮送詣京師。

translations.literal: When Zheng reached Cizhou he encountered the former Eastern Palace Thousand-Bolt Li Zhian and the Prince of Qi's Guard Commander Li Sixing, shackled and being escorted to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Cizhou he met Li Zhian, former thousand-bolt officer of the Eastern Palace, and Li Sixing, guard commander of the Prince of Qi, shackled and bound for the capital.

sentences.zh: 徵謂副使李桐客曰：「吾等受命之日，前宮、齊府左右，皆令赦原不問。

translations.literal: Zheng said to his deputy Li Tongke, "From the day we received our commission, all retainers of the former Eastern Palace and Qi mansion were ordered pardoned and not to be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng told his deputy Li Tongke, "From the day of our commission, all retainers of the former Eastern Palace and the Prince of Qi were to be pardoned without question.

sentences.zh: 今復送思行，此外誰不自疑？

translations.literal: If now we again send Sixing onward, who among the rest will not doubt himself?
translations.idiomatic: If we now send Sixing on, who else will not fear for himself?

sentences.zh: 徒遣使往，彼必不信，此乃差之毫釐，失之千里。

translations.literal: Sending envoys alone would not win belief — this would be missing by a hair's breadth and losing by a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy alone would not be believed — a hair's breadth of error becomes a thousand li of loss.

sentences.zh: 且公家之利，知無不爲，寧可慮身，不可廢國家大計。

translations.literal: Moreover the interest of the house is to do whatever one knows should be done; one may weigh personal safety, but one must not abandon the great plan of state.
translations.idiomatic: The state's interest demands action; personal safety may be weighed, but the nation's plan must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今若釋遣思行，不問其罪，則信義所感，無遠不臻。

translations.literal: If we now release Sixing and do not punish his offense, then the power of faith and righteousness will move all, however far.
translations.idiomatic: Release Sixing without punishment, and faith and righteousness will reach to the farthest corners.

sentences.zh: 古者，大夫出疆，苟利社稷，專之可也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when a grandee went beyond the frontier, if it benefited the altars of soil and grain he might decide the matter on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a minister abroad, if the altars of state required it, might decide on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 況今日之行，許以便宜從事，主上既以國士見待，安可不以國士報之乎？」

translations.literal: How much more today's mission, authorized to act as expedient circumstances require — since the sovereign already treats us as men of the state, how can we fail to repay him as men of the state?"
translations.idiomatic: How much more this mission, expressly authorized to act at discretion — if the emperor treats us as men of the state, how can we answer with less?"

sentences.zh: 即釋遣思行等，仍以啟聞，太宗甚悅。

translations.literal: He immediately released Sixing and the others, reported what he had done, and Taizong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He released Sixing and the others at once, reported his action, and Taizong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 太宗新即位，勵精政道，數引徵入臥內，訪以得失。

translations.literal: When Taizong had newly ascended the throne, he applied himself to government and repeatedly summoned Zheng into his private quarters to inquire about gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Newly enthroned, Taizong threw himself into government and often summoned Zheng to his private quarters to ask what was going wrong.

sentences.zh: 徵雅有經國之才，性又抗直，無所屈撓。

translations.literal: Zheng was by nature possessed of talent for ordering the state, and his character was also upright and unyielding, bending to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had genuine talent for governing, and his nature was blunt and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 太宗與之言，未嘗不欣然納受。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizong spoke with him, he never failed to accept his words with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong never failed to accept his counsel gladly.

sentences.zh: 徵亦喜逢知己之主，思竭其用，知無不言。

translations.literal: Zheng also rejoiced to meet a lord who knew his worth and bent every effort to serve him, speaking out on whatever he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, for his part, rejoiced to serve a ruler who knew his worth and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗勞之曰：「卿所陳諫，前後二百餘事，非卿至誠奉國，何能若是？」

translations.literal: Taizong once praised him, saying, "The remonstrances you have presented, more than two hundred in all — had you not served the state with utmost sincerity, how could it be so?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once praised him: "You have remonstrated more than two hundred times — without utmost loyalty to the state, how could you have done so?"

sentences.zh: 其年，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was promoted to left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 或有言徵阿黨親戚者，帝使御史大夫溫彥博案驗無狀，彥博奏曰：「徵爲人臣，須存形跡，不能遠避嫌疑，遂招此謗。

translations.literal: When someone said Zheng showed favoritism toward kinsmen, the emperor had Censor-in-Chief Wen Yanbo investigate and found no basis; Yanbo memorialized, saying, "Zheng, as a minister, ought to preserve visible propriety; failing to keep far from suspicion, he has brought on this slander.
translations.idiomatic: When someone accused Zheng of favoring relatives, the emperor had Censor-in-Chief Wen Yanbo investigate and found nothing; Yanbo reported, "As a minister, Zheng should keep clear of suspicion; by failing to do so he has invited this slander.

sentences.zh: 雖情在無私，亦有可責。」

translations.literal: Though his feelings are without private motive, he is still open to reproach."
translations.idiomatic: His motives may be pure, but he is still at fault."

sentences.zh: 帝令彥博讓徵，且曰：「自今後不得不存形跡。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yanbo to reprove Zheng and also said, "From now on you must preserve visible propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Yanbo rebuke Zheng and added, "From now on you must keep your conduct above reproach."

sentences.zh: 他日，徵入奏曰：「臣聞君臣協契，義同一體。

translations.literal: Another day Zheng entered to memorialize, saying, "Your subject has heard that when ruler and minister are in accord, their righteousness is one body.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Zheng memorialized, "Ruler and minister in accord are one body in duty.

sentences.zh: 不存公道，唯事形跡，若君臣上下，同遵此路，則邦之興喪，或未可知。」

translations.literal: If one does not uphold public right but cares only for visible propriety, and if ruler and minister above and below all follow this path, then whether the state rises or falls may be unknowable."
translations.idiomatic: If we care for appearances rather than public right, and ruler and ministers all follow that path, the fate of the state is unknowable."

sentences.zh: 帝瞿然改容曰：「吾已悔之。」

translations.literal: The emperor started and changed countenance, saying, "I already regret it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said, "I already regret that."

sentences.zh: 徵再拜曰：「願陛下使臣爲良臣，勿使臣爲忠臣。」

translations.literal: Zheng bowed again and said, "I wish Your Majesty would make me a good minister and not make me a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng bowed again: "Make me a good minister, not a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「忠、良有異乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Are loyal and good different?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Are loyal and good different?"

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「良臣，稷、契、咎陶是也。

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Good ministers were Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Good ministers were Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao.

sentences.zh: 忠臣，龍逢、比干是也。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers were Long Feng and Bi Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers were Long Feng and Bi Gan.

sentences.zh: 良臣使身獲美名，君受顯號，子孫傳世，福祿無疆。

translations.literal: Good ministers win fine reputations for themselves, lofty titles for their lords, and their descendants inherit honor — blessings and emoluments without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Good ministers win honor for themselves and glory for their lord; their descendants inherit rank and endless reward.

sentences.zh: 忠臣身受誅夷，君陷大惡，家國並喪，空有其名。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers themselves suffer execution, their lords fall into great evil, house and state perish together, and they keep only empty names.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers die by the sword, their lords sink into ruin, house and state perish together, and only the name remains.

sentences.zh: 以此而言，相去遠矣。」

translations.literal: Spoken thus, the distance between them is far."
translations.idiomatic: By that measure the distance between them is vast."

sentences.zh: 帝深納其言，賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted his words and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his words to heart and gave him five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，遷秘書監，參預朝政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and participated in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 he became director of the Secretariat and joined deliberations of state.

sentences.zh: 徵以喪亂之後，典章紛雜，奏引學者校定四部書。

translations.literal: Zheng, considering that after the disorders the canonical regulations were tangled, memorialized to summon scholars to collate the books of the Four Categories.
translations.idiomatic: After the civil wars had left the canon in disorder, Zheng had scholars collate the books of the four categories.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，秘府圖籍，粲然畢備。

translations.literal: Within a few years the palace library's charts and records were brilliantly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the palace library was fully restored.

sentences.zh: 時高昌王麹文泰將入朝，西域諸國咸欲因文泰遣使貢獻，太宗令文泰使人厭怛紇干往迎接之。

translations.literal: At that time King Qu Wentai of Gaochang was about to enter court, and all the states of the Western Regions wished to send envoys with tribute through Wentai; Taizong ordered Wentai's envoy Yantuo to go meet them.
translations.idiomatic: When King Qu Wentai of Gaochang was preparing to visit court, other Western Region states wished to send tribute through him; Taizong sent Wentai's envoy Yantuo to receive them.

sentences.zh: 徵諫曰：「中國始平，瘡痍未復，若微有勞役，則不自安。

translations.literal: Zheng remonstrated, saying, "The central lands have only just been pacified and the wounds are not yet healed; if there is even slight corvée labor, the people will not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng remonstrated: "The heartland has only just been pacified and the wounds are not healed; the slightest corvée will unsettle the people.

sentences.zh: 往年文泰入朝，所經州縣，猶不能供，況加於此輩。

translations.literal: In former years when Wentai entered court, the prefectures and counties he passed through still could not supply him — how much more if these peoples are added.
translations.idiomatic: When Wentai came before, the counties on his route could barely supply him — how much less if these peoples are added.

sentences.zh: 若任其商賈來往，邊人則獲其利；

translations.literal: If they are allowed to come and go as merchants, the border people will gain profit;
translations.idiomatic: Let them come as traders and the border people profit;

sentences.zh: 若爲賓客，中國即受其弊矣。

translations.literal: if they are received as guests, the central lands will suffer the harm.
translations.idiomatic: receive them as state guests and the heartland bears the cost.

sentences.zh: 漢建武二十二年，天下已寧。

translations.literal: In Han, in the twenty-second year of Jianwu, the realm was already at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, in Jianwu 22 the realm was already at peace.

sentences.zh: 西域請置都護、送侍子，光武不許，蓋不以蠻夷勞弊中國也。

translations.literal: The Western Regions requested a Protector-General and to send hostage sons; Guangwu did not permit it, considering that the barbarians should not weary and harm the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions asked for a protector-general and to send hostage sons; Emperor Guangwu refused, unwilling to burden China for barbarian sake.

sentences.zh: 今若許十國入貢，其使不下千人，欲使緣邊諸州何以取濟？

translations.literal: If ten states are now allowed to enter tribute, their envoys will be no fewer than a thousand — how are the border prefectures to provide for them?
translations.idiomatic: If ten states send tribute, their envoys will number at least a thousand — how will the border prefectures feed them?

sentences.zh: 人心萬端，後雖悔之，恐無所及。」

translations.literal: Human hearts are endlessly varied; though one may regret it later, I fear there will be no remedy."
translations.idiomatic: Hearts are fickle; regret later will come too late."

sentences.zh: 上善其議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 時厭怛紇干已發，遽追止之。

translations.literal: Yantuo had already set out; he was urgently recalled and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yantuo had already departed and was urgently recalled.

sentences.zh: 後太宗幸九成宮，因有宮人還京，憩於湋川縣之官舍。

translations.literal: Later Taizong visited Jiucheng Palace; because palace women were returning to the capital, they rested at the government guesthouse in Weichuan county.
translations.idiomatic: Later, visiting Jiucheng Palace, Taizong learned that palace women returning to the capital had rested at the Weichuan county guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 俄又右僕射李靖、侍中王珪繼至，官屬移宮人於別所而舍靖等。

translations.literal: Soon Right Vice Director Li Jing and Palace Attendant Wang Gui also arrived; the officials moved the palace women elsewhere and lodged Jing and the others in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Li Jing and Palace Attendant Wang Gui arrived soon after; officials moved the women out and gave their quarters to Jing and Gui.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，怒曰：「威福之柄，豈由靖等？

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it he angrily said, "Are the handles of authority and favor in Jing's hands?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard and angrily said, "Do the handles of power and favor belong to Jing?

sentences.zh: 何爲禮靖而輕我宮人！」

translations.literal: Why honor Jing and slight my palace women!"
translations.idiomatic: Why honor Jing and slight my palace women!"

sentences.zh: 即令案驗湋川官屬及靖等。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered an investigation of the Weichuan officials and of Jing and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an investigation of the Weichuan officials and of Jing and the others.

sentences.zh: 徵諫曰：「靖等，陛下心膂大臣；

translations.literal: Zheng remonstrated, saying, "Jing and the others are Your Majesty's backbone ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng remonstrated: "Jing and the others are Your Majesty's chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 宮人，皇后掃除之隸。

translations.literal: the palace women are the empress's sweepers and menials.
translations.idiomatic: the palace women are the empress's household staff.

sentences.zh: 論其委付，事理不同。

translations.literal: Judging by the trust reposed in them, the principle is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: By the trust reposed in them, the cases differ.

sentences.zh: 又靖等出外，官吏訪朝廷法式，歸來，陛下問人間疾苦。

translations.literal: Moreover when Jing and the others go abroad, officials inquire about court law; when they return, Your Majesty asks about the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and others travel, local officials ask about court law; when they return, Your Majesty asks about the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 靖等自當與官吏相見，官吏亦不可不謁也。

translations.literal: Jing and the others ought naturally to meet officials, and officials cannot fail to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: They must meet officials, and officials must receive them.

sentences.zh: 至於宮人，供食之外，不合參承。

translations.literal: As for palace women, apart from supplying food they ought not to be received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women, apart from serving meals, should not be received in audience.

sentences.zh: 若以此罪責縣吏，恐不益德音，徒駭天下耳目。」

translations.literal: If the county officials are punished on this account, I fear it will not enhance Your virtuous reputation but will only startle the ears of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Punishing the county officials for this will not enhance Your reputation — it will only alarm the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 乃釋官吏之罪，李靖等亦寢而不問。

translations.literal: He then released the officials from punishment, and Li Jing and the others were also left uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: He released the officials from blame and dropped the matter against Li Jing and the others.

sentences.zh: 尋宴於丹霄樓，酒酣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward there was a banquet in Danxiao Tower; when the wine had gone deep.
translations.idiomatic: Soon there was a banquet in Danxiao Tower; when the wine had gone deep,

sentences.zh: 太宗謂長孫無忌曰：「魏徵、王珪，昔在東宮，盡心所事，當時誠亦可惡。

translations.literal: Taizong said to Zhangsun Wuji, "Wei Zheng and Wang Gui, formerly in the Eastern Palace, gave their whole hearts to whom they served — at the time they were indeed hateful.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to Zhangsun Wuji, "Wei Zheng and Wang Gui served the Eastern Palace with all their hearts — at the time they were hateful enough.

sentences.zh: 我能拔擢用之，以至今日，足爲無愧古人。

translations.literal: That I could raise and employ them until today is enough to be without shame before the men of old.
translations.idiomatic: That I could raise and use them until today is enough to face the ancients without shame.

sentences.zh: 然徵毎諫我不從，發言輒即不應，何也？」

translations.literal: Yet whenever Zheng remonstrates and I do not follow, he speaks and then at once does not answer — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Zheng remonstrates and I do not follow, he falls silent — why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣以事有不可，所以陳論，若不從輒應，便恐此事即行。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject finds that when a matter cannot be done, that is why he states his view; if Your Majesty did not follow and he at once answered, he would fear the matter would immediately be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied, "When a matter should not be done, I say so; if Your Majesty did not follow and I answered at once, I would fear the matter would proceed."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「但當時且應，更別陳論，豈不得耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "But if you answered at the time and then stated your view separately, would that not do?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But if you answered at the time and argued afterward, would that not do?"

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「昔舜誡群臣：『爾無面從，退有後言。』

translations.literal: Zheng said, "In former times Shun admonished his ministers: 'Do not agree to my face and speak afterward behind my back.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Shun warned his ministers: 'Do not agree to my face and speak behind my back.

sentences.zh: 若臣面從陛下方始諫，此即『退有後言』，豈是稷、契事堯、舜之意耶？」

translations.literal: If your subject agreed to Your Majesty's face and only then remonstrated, that would be 'speaking afterward behind your back' — how would that be the intent of Ji and Qi in serving Yao and Shun?"
translations.idiomatic: If I agreed to Your face and remonstrated only afterward, that would be 'speaking behind your back' — is that how Ji and Qi served Yao and Shun?""

sentences.zh: 帝大笑曰：「人言魏徵舉動疎慢，我但覺嫵媚，適爲此耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and said, "People say Wei Zheng's bearing is rough and careless, but I only find him charming — it is just for this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong laughed: "People say Zheng is rough, but I find him delightful — this is why."

sentences.zh: 徵拜謝曰：「陛下導之使言，臣所以敢諫，若陛下不受臣諫，豈敢數犯龍鱗？」

translations.literal: Zheng bowed in thanks and said, "Your Majesty guides us to speak — that is why your subject dares remonstrate; if Your Majesty did not accept your subject's remonstrance, how would he dare repeatedly touch the dragon's scales?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng bowed: "Your Majesty invites speech — that is why I dare remonstrate; if You did not accept it, how could I touch the dragon's scales?"

sentences.zh: 是月，長樂公主將出降，帝以皇后所生，敕有司資送倍於永嘉長公主。

translations.literal: That month Princess Changle was about to marry; because she was born of the empress, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to supply her dowry at double that of Princess Yongjia the Elder.
translations.idiomatic: That month Princess Changle was to marry; as the empress's daughter, the emperor ordered a dowry double that of the Elder Princess Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Zheng said, "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "That cannot be.

sentences.zh: 昔漢明欲封其子，云『我子豈與先帝子等？

translations.literal: In former times when Emperor Ming of Han wished to enfeoff his son, he said, 'Are my sons to be equal to the Former Emperor's sons?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Han, enfeoffing his son, said, 'Are my sons equal to the late emperor's sons?

sentences.zh: 可半楚、淮陽。』

translations.literal: They may have half of Chu and Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Let them have half of Chu and Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 前史以爲美談。

translations.literal: Former histories took this as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: History praises this.

sentences.zh: 天子姊妹爲長公主，子爲公主，既加『長』字，即是有所尊崇。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's sisters are elder princesses; sons are princesses — since the word 'elder' is added, that itself shows honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's sisters are elder princesses; his daughters are princesses — the word 'elder' itself marks honor.

sentences.zh: 或可情有淺深，無容禮相踰越。」

translations.literal: Affection may run deep or shallow, but ritual must not be exceeded.""
translations.idiomatic: Affection may differ, but ritual must not be exceeded.""

sentences.zh: 上然其言，入告長孫皇后，後遣使齎錢四十萬、絹四百匹，詣徵宅以賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, entered and told Empress Zhangsun; the empress sent envoys with four hundred thousand cash and four hundred bolts of silk to Zheng's house as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, told Empress Zhangsun, and she sent four hundred thousand cash and four hundred bolts of silk to Zheng's house.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵郡公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was advanced in rank to Duke of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to duke of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 七年，代王珪爲侍中，尚書省滯訟有不決者，詔徵評理之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he replaced Wang Gui as Palace Attendant; for lawsuits stalled in the Department of State Affairs that could not be decided, an edict ordered Zheng to judge them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he replaced Wang Gui as palace attendant; stalled lawsuits in the Department of State Affairs were referred to him for judgment.

sentences.zh: 徵性非習法，但存大體，以情處斷，無不悅服。

translations.literal: Zheng's nature was not trained in law, but he kept to the larger pattern and decided according to human feeling — none failed to accept with satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Untrained in law, he judged by principle and human feeling — and all accepted his decisions.

sentences.zh: 初，有詔遣令狐德棻、岑文本撰《周史》，孔穎達、許敬宗撰《隋史》，姚思廉撰《梁》、《陳史》，李百藥撰《齊史》。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had ordered Linghu Defen and Cen Wenben to compile the History of Zhou, Kong Yingda and Xu Jingzong to compile the History of Sui, Yao Silian to compile the Histories of Liang and Chen, and Li Baiyao to compile the History of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had assigned Linghu Defen and Cen Wenben the History of Zhou, Kong Yingda and Xu Jingzong the History of Sui, Yao Silian the histories of Liang and Chen, and Li Baiyao the History of Qi.

sentences.zh: 徵受詔總加撰定，多所損益，薦在簡正。

translations.literal: Zheng received an edict to oversee and finalize the compilation, making many additions and deletions, all kept concise and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was ordered to oversee the compilation, revising heavily for clarity and correctness.

sentences.zh: 《隋史》序論，皆徵所作、《梁》、《陳》、《齊》各爲總論，時稱良史。

translations.literal: The introductory essays of the History of Sui were all composed by Zheng; for Liang, Chen, and Qi he wrote general essays each — at the time they were called good histories.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the introductory essays of the History of Sui and general essays for Liang, Chen, and Qi — histories praised as models.

sentences.zh: 史成，加左光祿大夫，進封鄭國公，賜物二千段。

translations.literal: When the histories were completed, he was made Left Grand Master of the Palace and advanced to Duke of Zheng, with two thousand lengths of goods as gift.
translations.idiomatic: When the histories were finished he was made left grand master of the palace, promoted to Duke of Zheng, and given two thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 徵自以無功於國，徒以辯説，遂參帷幄，深懼滿盈，後以目疾頻表遜位。

translations.literal: Zheng himself considered that he had no merit to the state and had entered the inner councils only through argument — he deeply feared reaching fullness and overflow; later, because of eye disease, he repeatedly memorialized to yield his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng felt he had won office by argument alone and, fearing excess, repeatedly asked to retire on account of eye disease.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕拔卿於讎虜之中，任公以樞要之職，見朕之非，未嘗不諫。

translations.literal: Taizong said, "I raised you from among enemy captives and entrusted you with a pivotal office; whenever you saw my faults you never failed to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I raised you from among enemies and gave you a pivotal post; you never failed to correct my faults.

sentences.zh: 公獨不見金之在礦也，何足貴哉？

translations.literal: Do you alone not see that gold in the ore — what is there to prize in it?
translations.idiomatic: Gold in the ore — what is it worth?

sentences.zh: 良冶鍛而爲器，便爲人所寶，朕方自比於金，以卿爲良匠。

translations.literal: When a good smith forges it into an implement, it becomes what men treasure; I am just now comparing myself to gold and you to the good smith.
translations.idiomatic: Forged by a good smith it becomes treasure; I compare myself to the ore and you to the smith.

sentences.zh: 卿雖有疾，未爲衰老，豈得便爾？」

translations.literal: Though you have illness, you are not yet old — how can you leave so?"
translations.idiomatic: You are ill but not old — how can you leave so soon?"

sentences.zh: 其年，徵又面請遜位，太宗難違之，乃拜徵特進，仍知門下事。

translations.literal: That year Zheng again requested in person to yield his post; Taizong found it hard to refuse and appointed Zheng Supernumerary Counselor, still directing affairs of the Department of the Chancellery as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year he asked again in person; Taizong made him supernumerary counselor while he continued to direct the Department of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 其後又頻上四疎，以陳得失。

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly submitted four memorials setting forth gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted four memorials on the state of governance.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：

translations.literal: The first reads:
translations.idiomatic: The first reads:

sentences.zh: 其二曰：

translations.literal: The second reads:
translations.idiomatic: The second reads:

sentences.zh: 其三曰：

translations.literal: The third reads:
translations.idiomatic: The third reads:

sentences.zh: 夫鑑形之美惡，必就於止水；

translations.literal: To mirror the beauty or ugliness of a form, one must go to still water;
translations.idiomatic: To see whether a face is fair or foul, one looks into still water;

sentences.zh: 鑑國之安危，必取於亡國。

translations.literal: to mirror a state's safety or peril, one must take a fallen state.
translations.idiomatic: to judge a state's safety or peril, one takes a fallen state as mirror.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「殷鑑不遠，在夏後之世。」

translations.literal: The Odes say, "The mirror of Yin is not far — it is in the age of the Xia successor."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "The mirror of Yin is not far — it is in the age after Xia."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「伐柯伐柯，其則不遠。」

translations.literal: It also says, "Cutting a handle, cutting a handle — the pattern is not far."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Cutting a handle, cutting a handle — the model is near at hand."

sentences.zh: 臣願當今之動靜，思隋氏以爲鑑，則存亡治亂，可得而知。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that in today's movements and stillness you would take the Sui as mirror — then survival and destruction, order and disorder, may be known.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that in all You do today You take the Sui as mirror — then survival, destruction, order, and chaos may be known.

sentences.zh: 若能思其所以危，則安矣；

translations.literal: If one can think on what brought peril, then there will be safety;
translations.idiomatic: Think on what brought peril and there will be safety;

sentences.zh: 思其所以亂，則治矣；

translations.literal: think on what brought disorder, then there will be order;
translations.idiomatic: think on what brought disorder and there will be order;

sentences.zh: 思其所以亡，則存矣。

translations.literal: think on what brought destruction, then there will be survival.
translations.idiomatic: think on what brought destruction and there will be survival.

sentences.zh: 存亡之所在，節嗜欲以從人。

translations.literal: Where survival and destruction lie, temper desires and follow the people.
translations.idiomatic: Survival lies in restraining desire and following the people.

sentences.zh: 省畋游之娛，息靡麗之作，罷不急之務，慎偏聽之怒。

translations.literal: Reduce the pleasure of hunting excursions, cease extravagant and beautiful works, drop tasks that are not urgent, and be careful of partial listening and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Cut hunting, cease luxury, drop non-urgent tasks, and guard against partial hearing and anger.

sentences.zh: 近忠厚，遠便佞，杜悅耳之邪説，聽苦口之忠言。

translations.literal: Draw near to honest generosity, keep far from clever flattery, shut out pleasing but wicked talk, and listen to bitter but loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: Keep honest men near, flatterers far; reject pleasing falsehood, hear bitter truth.

sentences.zh: 去易進之人，賤難得之貨。

translations.literal: Remove men who advance easily, and treat lightly goods hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Remove easy climbers; treat rare goods lightly.

sentences.zh: 采堯、舜之誹謗，追禹、湯之罪己，惜十家之產，順百姓之心。

translations.literal: Adopt Yao and Shun's boards for criticism, follow Yu and Tang in confessing fault, cherish the livelihood of ten households, and accord with the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Take Yao and Shun's boards of criticism, Yu and Tang's confession of fault, spare ten households' livelihood, and follow the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 近取諸身，恕以待物。

translations.literal: Take from what is near in oneself and treat things with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Measure others by oneself and treat them with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 思勞謙以受益，不自滿以招損。

translations.literal: Think that labor and humility bring benefit, and that self-satisfaction invites loss.
translations.idiomatic: Know that humility brings gain and complacency brings loss.

sentences.zh: 有動則庶類以和，出言而千里斯應，超上德於前載，樹風聲於後昆。

translations.literal: When there is action, the myriad kinds are harmonized; when words go forth, a thousand li respond — surpassing the highest virtue of former ages and planting a reputation for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Act, and the myriad things harmonize; speak, and the realm answers — surpassing former sages and planting fame for posterity.

sentences.zh: 此聖哲之宏規，帝王之盛業，能事斯畢，在乎慎守而已。

translations.literal: This is the great pattern of sages and sage-emperors, the flourishing achievement of emperors and kings — once the work is done, it lies in careful preservation alone.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sage-emperor's great pattern — and once achieved, it rests on careful preservation alone.

sentences.zh: 夫守之則易，取之實難，既得其所以難，豈不能保其所以易？

translations.literal: To preserve is easy; to acquire is truly hard — having grasped what made acquisition hard, how can one not keep what makes preservation easy?
translations.idiomatic: Preserving is easy; winning is hard — having learned how hard winning is, can You not keep what is easy to preserve?

sentences.zh: 其或保之不固，則驕奢淫泆動之也。

translations.literal: If preservation is not firm, then arrogance, luxury, dissipation, and excess move it.
translations.idiomatic: If preservation fails, arrogance, luxury, and excess undo it.

sentences.zh: 慎終如始，可不勉歟！

translations.literal: To be careful at the end as at the beginning — can one not strive for this!
translations.idiomatic: Be as careful at the end as at the beginning — can You not strive for this!

sentences.zh: 《易》云：「君子安不忘危，存不忘亡，治不忘亂，是以身安而國家可保。」

translations.literal: The Changes say, "The noble man in security does not forget peril, in survival does not forget destruction, in order does not forget disorder — thus his person is secure and the state can be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes say, "The noble man in safety does not forget danger, in survival does not forget ruin, in order does not forget chaos — thus his person is secure and the state preserved."

sentences.zh: 誠哉斯言，不可以不深察也。

translations.literal: Truly these words — they cannot but be deeply examined.
translations.idiomatic: These words cannot be examined too deeply.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下欲善之志，不減於昔時，聞過必改，少虧於曩日。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's will to do good is no less than in former times, but in hearing of faults and correcting them you fall somewhat short of earlier days.
translations.idiomatic: Your will to do good is no less than before, but You hear faults and correct them somewhat less readily than once.

sentences.zh: 若能以當今之無事，行疇昔之恭儉，則盡善盡美，固無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: If with today's peace you could practice the reverence and frugality of former days, then perfection would be complete — there would truly be nothing left to praise.
translations.idiomatic: If in today's peace You practiced the reverence and frugality of earlier days, perfection would be complete — nothing would remain to praise.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：

translations.literal: The fourth reads:
translations.idiomatic: The fourth reads:

sentences.zh: 夫君能盡禮，臣得竭忠，必在於內外無私，上下相信。

translations.literal: That ruler and minister can fulfill ritual and minister can exhaust loyalty must lie in having no private interest within or without and in mutual trust above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister can fulfill ritual and loyalty only when neither harbors private interest and both trust each other.

sentences.zh: 上不信則無以使下，下不信則無以事上。

translations.literal: If the superior does not trust, he has no means to employ those below; if those below do not trust, they have no means to serve the superior.
translations.idiomatic: Without trust above, the ruler cannot employ men below; without trust below, ministers cannot serve.

sentences.zh: 信之爲義，大矣哉！

translations.literal: The meaning of trust — how great it is!
translations.idiomatic: How great is the meaning of trust!

sentences.zh: 故自天祐之，吉無不利。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven assists it, and good fortune attends without harm.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven assists it, and fortune comes without harm.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公問於管仲曰：「吾欲酒腐於爵，肉腐於俎，得無害於霸乎？」

translations.literal: In former times Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong, saying, "I wish my wine to rot in the goblet and my meat to rot on the stand — would that harm hegemony?
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong, "If my wine rots in the cup and my meat on the tray, would that harm hegemony?"

sentences.zh: 管仲曰：「此極非其善者，然亦無害霸也。」

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said, "This is extremely not among the good, yet it also does not harm hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said, "That is far from good, yet it would not harm hegemony either."

sentences.zh: 公曰：「何如而害霸乎？」

translations.literal: The duke said, "What would harm hegemony?
translations.idiomatic: The duke asked, "What would harm hegemony?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不能知人，害霸也；

translations.literal: He said, "Not knowing men harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Not knowing men harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 知而不能用，害霸也；

translations.literal: knowing but not using harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: knowing them but not using them harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 用而不能信，害霸也；

translations.literal: using but not trusting harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: using them but not trusting them harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 既信而又使小人參之，害霸也。」

translations.literal: having trusted yet letting petty men share in it harms hegemony."
translations.idiomatic: and trusting them yet letting petty men interfere harms hegemony."

sentences.zh: 晉中行穆伯攻鼓，經年而不能下，饋間倫曰：「鼓之嗇夫，間倫知之，請無疲士大夫而鼓可得。」

translations.literal: In Jin, Mu Bo of Zhonghang attacked Gu, and for a year could not take it; Jian Lun of Kui said, "Gu's intendant — Jian Lun knows him; please do not weary the officers and gentlemen and Gu can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Mu Bo of Zhonghang besieged Gu for a year without success; Jian Lun of Kui said, "I know Gu's intendant — do not weary the officers and Gu can be taken."

sentences.zh: 穆伯不應。

translations.literal: Mu Bo did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Bo did not answer.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「不折一戟，不傷一卒，而鼓可得，君奚爲不取？」

translations.literal: Those at his side said, "Without breaking a single halberd or wounding a single soldier, yet Gu can be taken — why does my lord not accept?
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "Not a halberd broken nor a soldier hurt, yet Gu can be taken — why not accept?"

sentences.zh: 穆伯曰：「間倫之爲人也，佞而不仁。

translations.literal: Mu Bo said, "Jian Lun's character is flattery without humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Bo said, "Jian Lun is flatterer and inhumane.

sentences.zh: 若間倫下之，吾不可以不賞。

translations.literal: If Jian Lun took Gu, I could not fail to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: If Jian Lun took Gu, I would have to reward him.

sentences.zh: 賞之，是賞佞人也。

translations.literal: To reward him would be to reward a flatterer.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarding him would reward a flatterer.

sentences.zh: 佞人得志，是使晉國之士舍仁而爲佞，雖得鼓，將何用之？」

translations.literal: If flatterers got their way, it would make the officers of Jin abandon humaneness and become flatterers — though Gu were taken, of what use would it be?"
translations.idiomatic: If flatterers prosper, Jin's officers will abandon humaneness for flattery — even with Gu, what would it profit?"

sentences.zh: 夫穆伯列國大夫，管仲霸者之佐，猶慎於信任，遠避佞人也如此，況乎爲四海之大君，應千齡之上聖，而可使巍巍之盛德，復將有所間然乎？

translations.literal: Mu Bo was a grandee of a feudal state and Guan Zhong the assistant of a hegemon — yet they were so careful in trust and so far from flatterers; how much more for the great lord of the four seas, answering to a sage of a thousand ages — can one let towering virtue again be marred?
translations.idiomatic: Mu Bo was a feudal grandee and Guan Zhong a hegemon's aide — yet they were so careful of trust and so wary of flatterers; how much more for the lord of the four seas and sage of a thousand ages — can towering virtue be marred?

sentences.zh: 若欲令君子小人是非不雜，必懷之以德，待之以信，厲之以義，節之以禮，然後善善而惡惡，審罰而明賞，則小人絶其佞邪，君子自強不息。

translations.literal: If you wish the noble and petty, right and wrong, not to be mixed, you must embrace them with virtue, treat them with trust, steel them with righteousness, and restrain them with ritual — then you will approve the good and hate the evil, examine punishments and clarify rewards, and petty men will cut off their flattery and wickedness while noble men strengthen themselves without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: To keep noble and petty, right and wrong, from mingling, embrace men with virtue, treat them with trust, steel them with righteousness, and restrain them with ritual — then approve the good, punish the evil, and petty men will cease their flattery while noble men strengthen themselves without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 無爲之化，何遠之有？

translations.literal: The transformation of non-action — how far can it be?
translations.idiomatic: Rule by non-action — how far off is it?

sentences.zh: 善善而不能進，惡惡而不能去，罰不及於有罪，賞不加於有功，則危亡之期，或未可保。

translations.literal: If you approve the good yet cannot advance it, hate the evil yet cannot remove it, punishments do not reach the guilty, and rewards do not fall on the meritorious, then the time of peril and destruction may not be kept off.
translations.idiomatic: If You approve the good yet cannot promote it, hate the evil yet cannot remove it, punish the guilty insufficiently, and fail to reward merit, peril may not be kept off.

sentences.zh: 永錫祚胤，將何望哉？

translations.literal: Forever bestowing blessings on descendants — upon what can one set hope?
translations.idiomatic: Forever bestowing blessings on Your line — upon what can one set hope?

sentences.zh: 太宗手詔嘉美，優納之。

translations.literal: Taizong wrote an edict in his own hand praising and favorably accepting them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote a personal edict praising and accepting them.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂長孫無忌曰：「朕即位之初，上書者或言『人主必須威權獨運，不得委任群下』；

translations.literal: He once said to Zhangsun Wuji, "At the beginning of my reign, some who submitted memorials said, 'The lord of men must exercise authority alone and must not delegate to the multitude below';
translations.idiomatic: He once told Zhangsun Wuji, "At the start of my reign some memorialists said, 'The ruler must wield power alone and not delegate to his ministers';

sentences.zh: 或欲耀兵振武，懾服四夷。

translations.literal: some wished to display troops and martial power to overawe the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: others wanted to display arms and overawe the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 唯有魏徵勸朕『偃革興文，布德施惠，中國既安，遠人自服』。

translations.literal: Only Wei Zheng urged me, 'Lay down arms and raise culture, spread virtue and bestow grace — when the central lands are secure, distant peoples will submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei Zheng urged me, 'Lay down arms and raise culture, spread virtue and grace — secure the heartland and distant peoples will submit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 朕從其語，天下大寧。

translations.literal: I followed his words, and the realm was greatly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I followed him, and the realm was greatly at peace.

sentences.zh: 絶域君長，皆來朝貢，九夷重譯，相望於道。

translations.literal: Lords of distant regions all came to court with tribute; the nine Yi, through repeated translation, followed one upon another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Distant lords came to court; barbarian envoys lined the roads with repeated translation.

sentences.zh: 此皆魏徵之力也。」

translations.literal: This is all the power of Wei Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: This is all Wei Zheng's doing.""

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗嫌上封者眾，不近事實，欲加黜責。

translations.literal: Taizong once resented the great number of sealed memorials, finding them not close to facts, and wished to demote and reprove the writers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once resented the flood of sealed memorials as unrealistic and wished to punish their authors.

sentences.zh: 徵奏曰：「古者立誹謗之木，欲聞己過。

translations.literal: Zheng memorialized, saying, "In antiquity they erected boards for slander, wishing to hear their own faults.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng memorialized: "Antiquity erected boards for slander because rulers wished to hear their faults.

sentences.zh: 今之封事，謗木之流也。

translations.literal: Today's sealed memorials are the stream of those boards.
translations.idiomatic: Today's sealed memorials are their lineal descendants.

sentences.zh: 陛下思聞得失，祗可恣其陳道。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to hear gains and losses — you should simply let them state their views freely.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to hear truth, let them speak freely.

sentences.zh: 若所言衷，則有益於陛下；

translations.literal: If what is said is sincere, then it benefits Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: If they are sincere, You benefit;

sentences.zh: 若不衷，無損於國家。」

translations.literal: if not sincere, it does no harm to the state."
translations.idiomatic: if not, the state is unharmed."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「此言是也。」

translations.literal: Taizong said, "These words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "That is right."

sentences.zh: 並勞而遣之。

translations.literal: He also comforted them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted the memorialists and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 後太宗在洛陽宮，幸積翠池，宴群臣，酒酣各賦一事。

translations.literal: Later Taizong was at Luoyang Palace, visited Jicui Pond, and banqueted the ministers; when the wine had gone deep each was to compose on one theme.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Luoyang Palace, at a banquet by Jicui Pond when wine had gone deep, each minister was to compose on a theme.

sentences.zh: 太宗賦《尚書》曰：「日昃玩百篇，臨燈披《五典》。

translations.literal: Taizong composed on the Documents, saying, "The sun declines and I enjoy the hundred chapters; by lamplight I unroll the Five Canons.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong composed on the Documents: "The sun declines and I enjoy the hundred chapters; by lamplight I unroll the Five Canons.

sentences.zh: 夏康既逸豫，商辛亦流湎。

translations.literal: Xia Kang already gave himself to ease; Shang Xin also drifted in indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Kang already gave himself to ease; Shang Xin drifted in indulgence.

sentences.zh: 恣情昏主多，克己明君鮮。

translations.literal: Self-indulgent dark lords are many; self-restraining enlightened lords are few.
translations.idiomatic: Dark lords who indulged themselves were many; enlightened lords who restrained themselves were few.

sentences.zh: 滅身資累惡，成名由積善。」

translations.literal: Destroying the person accumulates evil; achieving a name comes from accumulating good."
translations.idiomatic: Ruin the person by accumulated evil; win a name by accumulated good."

sentences.zh: 徵賦西漢曰：「受降臨軹道，爭長趣鴻門。

translations.literal: Zheng composed on Western Han, saying, "Receiving surrender at Zhidao, contending for precedence hurrying to Hong Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng composed on Western Han: "Receiving surrender at Zhidao, contending for precedence at Hong Gate.

sentences.zh: 驅傳渭橋上，觀兵細柳屯。

translations.literal: Driving relay at Weiqiao, reviewing troops at Xiiliu camp.
translations.idiomatic: Driving relay at Weiqiao, reviewing troops at Xiiliu camp.

sentences.zh: 夜宴經柏谷，朝游出杜原。

translations.literal: Feasting by night at Bai Valley, touring by day out of Du Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting by night at Bai Valley, touring by day from Du Plain.

sentences.zh: 終藉叔孫禮，方知皇帝尊。」

translations.literal: Only through Shusun's ritual did he know the emperor's honor."
translations.idiomatic: Only through Shusun Tong's ritual did he learn the emperor's honor."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「魏徵毎言，必約我以禮也。」

translations.literal: Taizong said, "Whenever Wei Zheng speaks, he must bind me with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Whenever Zheng speaks, he binds me with ritual."

sentences.zh: 尋以修定《五禮》，當封一子爲縣男，請讓孤兄子叔慈。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because of revising the Five Rites, when one son was to be enfeoffed as Baron of a county, he requested that the title go to his orphaned elder brother's son Shuci.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, when one son was to be enfeoffed for revising the Five Rites, he asked that the title go to his late elder brother's son Shuci.

sentences.zh: 太宗愴然曰：「卿之此心，可以勵俗。」

translations.literal: Taizong said with emotion, "Your heart in this can move custom.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said warmly, "This heart of yours can move custom."

sentences.zh: 遂許之。

translations.literal: He then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He granted the request.

sentences.zh: 十二年，禮部尚書王珪奏言：「三品以上遇親王於途，皆降乘，違法申敬，有乖儀准。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Minister of Rites Wang Gui memorialized, saying, "Officials of third rank and above, meeting imperial princes on the road, all dismount from their carriages — unlawfully showing respect, contrary to ritual standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Minister of Rites Wang Gui reported, "Officials of third rank and above dismount when meeting imperial princes on the road — an unlawful show of respect contrary to ritual."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「卿輩皆自崇貴，卑我兒子乎？」

translations.literal: Taizong said, "Are you gentlemen elevating yourselves and demeaning my sons?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Are you elevating yourselves and demeaning my sons?"

sentences.zh: 徵進曰：「自古迄茲，親王班次三公之下。

translations.literal: Zheng advanced and said, "From antiquity until now, imperial princes rank below the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied, "From antiquity until now imperial princes have ranked below the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 今三品皆曰天子列卿及八座之長，爲王降乘，非王所宜當也。

translations.literal: Now those of third rank are called the Son of Heaven's ranked ministers and chiefs of the Eight Seats — for princes to dismount is not what princes ought to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank officials are the Son of Heaven's chief ministers and heads of the eight seats — princes should not dismount for them.

sentences.zh: 求諸故事，則無可憑；

translations.literal: Seeking precedent, there is nothing to rely on;
translations.idiomatic: There is no precedent;

sentences.zh: 行之於今，又乖國憲。」

translations.literal: practicing it today again violates the constitution of state."
translations.idiomatic: and to practice it today violates the constitution."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「國家所以立太子者，擬以爲君也。

translations.literal: Taizong said, "The reason the state establishes a crown prince is that he is intended to become lord.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "The state establishes a crown prince because he is meant to become ruler.

sentences.zh: 然則人之修短，不在老少，設無太子，則母弟次立。

translations.literal: Yet a man's span is not in old or young; if there were no crown prince, then the younger brother by the same mother would succeed next.
translations.idiomatic: A man's worth is not in age; without a crown prince, a younger brother by the same mother succeeds next.

sentences.zh: 以此而言，安得輕我子耶？」

translations.literal: Spoken thus, how can one slight my sons?"
translations.idiomatic: By that logic, how can I slight my sons?"

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「殷家尚質，有兄終弟及之義；

translations.literal: Zheng said, "The house of Yin valued substance and had the principle of elder brother finishing and younger brother succeeding;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "The Yin valued substance and allowed a younger brother to succeed an elder brother;

sentences.zh: 自周以降，立嫡必長，所以絶庶孽之窺覦，塞禍亂之源本，有國者之所深慎。」

translations.literal: from Zhou downward, the established heir must be the eldest — thus to cut off the covetous glances of secondary sons and block the root source of calamity and disorder is what those who possess a state deeply guard."
translations.idiomatic: from Zhou onward the legitimate heir must be the eldest — to cut off secondary sons' ambitions and block the root of disorder is what every state deeply guards."

sentences.zh: 於是遂可珪奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gui's memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 會皇孫誕育，召公卿賜宴，太宗謂侍臣曰：「貞觀以前，從我平定天下，周旋艱險，玄齡之功，無所與讓。

translations.literal: When an imperial grandson was born, the emperor summoned the high ministers to a gift banquet and said to his attending ministers, "Before Zhenguan, in following me to settle the realm and threading through hardship, Xuanling's achievement — none could share it.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial grandson was born, Taizong banqueted the high ministers and said, "Before Zhenguan, in pacifying the realm through hardship, Xuanling's achievement had no rival.

sentences.zh: 貞觀之後，盡心於我，獻納忠讜，安國利民，犯顏正諫，匡朕之違者，唯魏徵而已。

translations.literal: After Zhenguan, giving his whole heart to me, offering loyal remonstrance, settling the state and benefiting the people, correcting my countenance and remonstrating against my errors — only Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenguan, giving his whole heart, offering loyal remonstrance, settling the state and benefiting the people, correcting my errors — only Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 古之名臣，何以加也！」

translations.literal: Compared with famous ministers of old, how can one add to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Compared with famous ministers of old, who could surpass him!"

sentences.zh: 於是親解佩刀以賜二人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally unfastened his belt knife and bestowed it on the two men.
translations.idiomatic: He personally unfastened his belt knife and gave it to the two men.

sentences.zh: 徵以戴聖《禮記》編次不倫，遂爲《類禮》二十捲，以類相從，削其重復，采先儒訓注，擇善從之，研精覃思，數年而畢。

translations.literal: Because Dai Sheng's Record of Rites was arranged out of order, Zheng therefore made Categorized Rites in twenty scrolls, arranging by category, cutting repetitions, selecting the best from earlier scholars' glosses and commentaries, and refining with deep thought — completed after several years.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Dai Sheng's Record of Rites poorly arranged, Zheng compiled Categorized Rites in twenty scrolls, grouping by topic, cutting repetition, and choosing the best earlier commentary — work of several years.

sentences.zh: 太宗覽而善之，賜物一千段，録數本以賜太子及諸王，仍藏之秘府。

translations.literal: Taizong read it and approved, bestowed a thousand lengths of goods, had several copies recorded and given to the crown prince and the princes, and still stored them in the secret treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved it, gave a thousand lengths of goods, had copies made for the crown prince and other princes, and stored the work in the secret treasury.

sentences.zh: 先是，遣使詣西域立葉護可汗，未還，又遣使多齎金銀帛歷諸國市馬。

translations.literal: Earlier envoys had been sent to the Western Regions to install Ashina as qaghan; before they returned, envoys were again sent carrying much gold, silk, and cloth to travel through the various states buying horses.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys had been sent to the Western Regions to install Ashina as qaghan; before they returned, more envoys were sent with gold, silk, and cloth to buy horses throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 徵諫曰：「今以立可汗爲名，可汗未定，即詣諸國市馬，彼必以爲意在市馬，不爲專意立可汗。

translations.literal: Zheng remonstrated, saying, "Now with installing the qaghan as the stated aim, before the qaghan is settled you already go to the various states to buy horses — they will surely think the intent is to buy horses and not to install the qaghan with single purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng remonstrated: "You name the mission installation of the qaghan, yet before he is settled You send men to buy horses — they will think You care for horses, not for installing the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 可汗得立，則不甚懷恩。

translations.literal: If the qaghan is installed, he will not greatly cherish the grace.
translations.idiomatic: If the qaghan is installed, he will not feel deep obligation.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃聞之，以爲中國薄義重利，未必得馬，而失義矣。

translations.literal: When the various barbarians hear of it, they will think the central lands value profit lightly and value righteousness poorly — horses may not be obtained, yet righteousness will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: The border peoples will think China values profit over faith — You may not get the horses and will lose righteousness.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文有獻千里馬者，曰：吾凶行日三十里，吉行五十里，鑾輿在前，屬車在後，吾獨乘千里馬將安之？

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Wen of Han, when someone presented a thousand-li horse, said, "On inauspicious days I travel thirty li, on auspicious days fifty li; with the imperial carriage before and the train of attendants behind, where would I ride a thousand-li horse alone?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han, offered a thousand-li horse, said, "On ill-omened days I travel thirty li, on good days fifty; with the imperial carriage before and attendants behind, where would I ride a thousand-li horse alone?

sentences.zh: 乃賞其道里所費而返之。

translations.literal: He therefore rewarded the cost of the journey and sent it back.
translations.idiomatic: He paid the journey's cost and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 漢光武有獻千里馬及寶劍者，馬以駕鼓車，劍以賜騎士。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han, when someone presented a thousand-li horse and a precious sword, used the horse to draw the drum carriage and gave the sword to a cavalryman.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu, offered a thousand-li horse and precious sword, used the horse for the drum carriage and gave the sword to a cavalryman.

sentences.zh: 陛下凡所施爲，皆邈逾三王之上，奈何至於此事，欲爲孝文、光武之下乎？

translations.literal: In everything Your Majesty does, you already far surpass the Three Kings — how can you in this matter wish to fall below Emperor Wen and Guangwu?
translations.idiomatic: In all You do You already surpass the Three Kings — why in this wish to fall below Wen and Guangwu?

sentences.zh: 又魏文帝欲求市西域大珠，蘇則曰：『若陛下惠及四海，則不求自至，求而得之，不足爲貴也。』

translations.literal: Moreover when Emperor Wen of Wei wished to buy a great pearl from the Western Regions, Su Ze said, 'If Your Majesty's grace reaches the four seas, it will come without seeking; what is obtained by seeking is not worth prizing.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei wished to buy a great pearl from the Western Regions, Su Ze said, 'If Your Majesty's grace reaches the four seas, it will come unbidden; what must be sought is not worth prizing.'

sentences.zh: 陛下縱不能慕漢文之高行，可不畏蘇則之言乎？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty may not be able to emulate Emperor Wen of Han's lofty conduct — can you not fear Su Ze's words?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may not emulate Emperor Wen of Han — can You not heed Su Ze's words?""

sentences.zh: 太宗納其言而止。

translations.literal: Taizong accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted and stopped the mission.

sentences.zh: 時公卿大臣並請封禪，唯徵以爲不可。

translations.literal: At that time the high ministers all requested the feng and shan rites; only Zheng thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the high ministers all urged the feng and shan rites, only Zheng opposed them.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕欲卿極言之。

translations.literal: Taizong said, "I wish you to speak to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Speak to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 豈功不高耶？

translations.literal: Is merit not high?
translations.idiomatic: Is my merit not high?

sentences.zh: 德不厚耶？

translations.literal: Is virtue not thick?
translations.idiomatic: Is my virtue not deep?

sentences.zh: 諸夏未治安耶？

translations.literal: Are the various Xia not yet governed in peace?
translations.idiomatic: Is the heartland not yet at peace?

sentences.zh: 遠夷不慕義耶？

translations.literal: Do distant barbarians not admire righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Do distant peoples not admire righteousness?

sentences.zh: 嘉瑞不至耶？

translations.literal: Have auspicious portents not arrived?
translations.idiomatic: Have auspicious omens not come?

sentences.zh: 年谷不登耶？

translations.literal: Have the year's grains not ripened?
translations.idiomatic: Have harvests not been good?

sentences.zh: 何爲而不可？」

translations.literal: Why can it not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Why then can it not be done?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下功則高矣，而民未懷惠；

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty's achievement is indeed high, yet the people have not yet felt grace;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied, "Your achievement is high, yet the people have not yet felt grace;

sentences.zh: 德雖厚矣，而澤未滂流；

translations.literal: though virtue is thick, its bounty has not yet poured abroad;
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue is deep, yet its bounty has not spread abroad;

sentences.zh: 諸夏雖安，未足以供事；

translations.literal: though the various Xia are at peace, they are not yet enough to supply the undertaking;
translations.idiomatic: the heartland is at peace, yet cannot bear the burden;

sentences.zh: 遠夷慕義，無以供其求；

translations.literal: though distant barbarians admire righteousness, there is not enough to meet their requests;
translations.idiomatic: distant peoples admire You, yet their demands cannot be met;

sentences.zh: 符瑞雖臻，網羅猶密；

translations.literal: though auspicious portents have come, the prisons remain crowded;
translations.idiomatic: though omens have come, the prisons remain crowded;

sentences.zh: 積歳豐稔，倉廩尚虛，此臣所以竊謂未可。

translations.literal: though years have heaped harvests, the granaries are still empty — this is why your subject privately says it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: though harvests have been good, the granaries are still empty — that is why I say it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 臣未能遠譬，且借喻於人。

translations.literal: Your subject cannot draw a far comparison and will borrow a likeness from a man.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot argue from distant examples — let me borrow a likeness from ordinary life.

sentences.zh: 今有人十年長患，療治且愈，此人應皮骨僅存，便欲使負米一石，日行百里，必不可得。

translations.literal: Suppose a man has been ill ten years; though treatment has nearly cured him, this person's flesh and bones barely remain — to make him carry a picul of rice and walk a hundred li in a day absolutely cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a man has been ill ten years; though treatment has nearly cured him, flesh and bone barely hold together — to make him carry a picul of rice and walk a hundred li in a day is impossible.

sentences.zh: 隋氏之亂，非止十年，陛下爲之良醫，疾苦雖已乂安，未甚充實，告成天地，臣竊有疑。

translations.literal: The disorder of the Sui house lasted more than ten years; Your Majesty has been its good physician — though the sickness is already settled, it is not yet fully replenished; to report completion to Heaven and Earth — your subject privately has doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's disorder lasted more than ten years; You have been the good physician — though the sickness is eased, the body is not yet restored; to report completion to Heaven and Earth, I have doubts.

sentences.zh: 且陛下東封，萬國咸萃，要荒之外，莫不奔走。

translations.literal: Moreover if Your Majesty performs the eastern feng, the myriad states will all gather; beyond the wilds and wastes, none will fail to hurry.
translations.idiomatic: If You perform the eastern feng, all states will gather; from the wilds none will fail to hurry.

sentences.zh: 今自伊、洛以東，暨乎海岱，灌莽巨澤，蒼茫千里，人煙斷絶，雞犬不聞，道路蕭條，進退艱阻，豈可引彼夷狄，示以虛弱？

translations.literal: Now from the Yi and Luo eastward to the sea and Mount Dai, through marshes and great lakes, for a thousand li in vast emptiness human smoke is broken off and neither cock nor dog is heard; the roads are desolate, advance and retreat difficult — how can you lead those barbarians and show them weakness?
translations.idiomatic: From the Yi and Luo eastward to the sea and Mount Dai, for a thousand li through marsh and waste, human habitation ceases and neither cock nor dog is heard; roads are desolate and travel hard — how can You lead barbarians there and show weakness?

sentences.zh: 竭財以賞，未厭遠人之望；

translations.literal: Exhausting wealth to reward them will not satisfy distant peoples' expectations;
translations.idiomatic: Exhausting wealth to reward them will not satisfy distant expectations;

sentences.zh: 重加給復，不償百姓之勞。

translations.literal: adding tax relief and remissions will not repay the people's labor.
translations.idiomatic: adding tax relief will not repay the people's labor.

sentences.zh: 或遇水旱之災，風雨之變，庸夫橫議，悔不可追。

translations.literal: If flood or drought disaster should come, or wind and rain change, the common man will speak rashly and regret will be irreversible.
translations.idiomatic: If flood, drought, or untimely weather follow, common talk will turn to regret with no remedy.

sentences.zh: 豈獨臣之懇誠，亦有輿人之誦。」

translations.literal: It is not your subject's earnest sincerity alone — there are also the songs of men in the marketplaces."
translations.idiomatic: This is not my earnestness alone — the marketplaces already murmur it."

sentences.zh: 太宗不能奪。

translations.literal: Taizong could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 是後，右僕射缺，欲拜之，徵固讓乃止。

translations.literal: Afterward the right vice director's post was vacant; the emperor wished to appoint him, but Zheng firmly declined and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the right vice directorship fell vacant, the emperor wished to appoint him, but Zheng firmly declined and the appointment stopped.

sentences.zh: 及皇太子承乾不修德業，魏王泰寵愛日隆，內外庶僚，並有疑議。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chengqian did not cultivate virtue and Prince Wei Tai's favor grew daily, officials within and without all had doubts.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chengqian neglected virtue and Prince Wei Tai's favor grew, officials inside and outside were uneasy.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而惡之，謂侍臣曰：「當今朝臣忠謇，無逾魏徵，我遣傅皇太子，用絶天下之望。」

translations.literal: When Taizong heard he was displeased and said to his attending ministers, "Among today's court ministers in loyal bluntness, none surpasses Wei Zheng; I send him to tutor the crown prince to cut off the realm's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, displeased, told his ministers, "Among today's blunt loyal ministers none surpasses Wei Zheng; I send him to tutor the crown prince and cut off the realm's false hopes."

sentences.zh: 十六年，拜太子太師，知門下省事如故。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, still directing affairs of the Department of the Chancellery as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made grand preceptor of the crown prince while continuing to direct the Department of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 徵自陳有疾，詔答曰：「漢之太子，四皓爲助，我之賴公，即其義也。

translations.literal: Zheng himself stated that he had illness; the edict replied, "In Han the crown prince had the Four Whiteheads as help — my reliance on you is that same principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng reported illness; the edict replied, "Han's crown prince had the Four Whiteheads as help — my reliance on you is the same.

sentences.zh: 知公疾病，可臥護之。」
