translations.literal: Knowing you are ill, you may tutor him from your bed."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing you are ill, tutor him from your bed."

sentences.zh: 其年，稱綿惙，中使相望。

translations.literal: That year he was said to be failing; palace envoys followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was failing; palace envoys came in succession.

sentences.zh: 徵宅先無正寢，太宗欲爲小殿，輟其材爲徵營構，五日而成，遣中使齎素褥布被而賜之，遂其所尚也。

translations.literal: Zheng's house originally had no main hall; Taizong wished to build a small hall and stopped its materials to construct one for Zheng — finished in five days — and sent a palace envoy with plain bedding and cotton quilts as gift, following what he valued.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's house had no main hall; Taizong halted materials for a small palace hall and built one for him in five days, sending plain bedding as Zheng preferred.

sentences.zh: 及病篤，輿駕再幸其第，撫之流涕，問所欲言，徵曰：「嫠不恤緯而憂宗周之亡。」

translations.literal: When his illness was critical, the imperial carriage twice visited his house; stroking him, Taizong wept and asked what he wished to say; Zheng said, "A widow does not grieve for her weaving but grieves for the fall of the royal house of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his crisis the emperor visited twice, wept, and asked his last words; Zheng said, "A widow does not grieve for her weaving but for the fall of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 後數日，太宗夜夢徵若平生，及旦而奏徵薨，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Several days later Taizong dreamed of Zheng as in life; at dawn came report that Zheng had died — he was sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Taizong dreamed of Zheng as in life; at dawn came word of his death — he was sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 太宗親臨慟哭，廢朝五日，贈司空、相州都督，謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: Taizong personally came and wailed; court was suspended five days; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and Area Commander of Xiangzhou, with posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong came in person and mourned; court was suspended five days; Zheng was posthumously made Minister of Works and area commander of Xiangzhou, with posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 給羽葆鼓吹、班劍四十人，賻絹布千段、米粟千石，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was given feather-canopy music, forty guards with swords, a thousand lengths of silk and cloth as funeral gifts, and a thousand piculs of grain and rice, and was buried near Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He received feather-canopy music, forty sword guards, a thousand lengths of silk and cloth, a thousand piculs of grain, and burial near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 及將祖載，徵妻裴氏曰：「徵平生儉素，今以一品禮葬，羽儀甚盛，非亡者之志。」

translations.literal: When the funeral procession was about to set out, Zheng's wife Lady Pei said, "Throughout his life Zheng was frugal and plain; now to bury him with first-rank ritual and such splendid guard is not the dead man's wish.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral was to set out, Lady Pei said, "Zheng lived frugally; first-rank burial with such splendor is not his wish."

sentences.zh: 悉辭不受，竟以布車載柩，無文彩之飾。

translations.literal: She declined all and would not accept, finally carrying the bier in a cloth carriage without ornamental decoration.
translations.idiomatic: She declined all honors and carried the bier in a plain cloth carriage without ornament.

sentences.zh: 太宗登苑西樓，望喪而哭，詔百官送出郊外。

translations.literal: Taizong ascended the western tower of the park, looked toward the funeral and wept, and ordered the hundred officials to escort it beyond the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong from the park's western tower watched the funeral and wept, and ordered officials to escort it beyond the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 帝親制碑文，並爲書石。

translations.literal: The emperor personally composed the inscription and also wrote the stone himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote the inscription and carved the stone himself.

sentences.zh: 其後追思不已，賜其實封九百戸。

translations.literal: Later, remembering him without cease, he granted his fief nine hundred households in actual revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Later, remembering him without cease, he granted his fief nine hundred households in actual revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘗臨朝謂侍臣曰：「夫以銅爲鏡，可以正衣冠；

translations.literal: He once at court said to his attending ministers, "Using bronze as a mirror, one can straighten cap and gown;
translations.idiomatic: He once told his ministers at court, "With bronze as mirror one can straighten cap and gown;

sentences.zh: 以古爲鏡，可以知興替；

translations.literal: using antiquity as a mirror, one can know rise and replacement;
translations.idiomatic: with antiquity as mirror one can know rise and fall;

sentences.zh: 以人爲鏡，可以明得失。

translations.literal: using men as a mirror, one can clarify gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: with men as mirror one can see gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 朕常保此三鏡，以防己過。

translations.literal: I constantly keep these three mirrors to guard against my faults.
translations.idiomatic: I keep these three mirrors to guard against my faults.

sentences.zh: 今魏徵殂逝，遂亡一鏡矣！

translations.literal: Now Wei Zheng has died — I have lost one mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Now Wei Zheng is dead — I have lost a mirror!

sentences.zh: 徵亡後，朕遣人至宅，就其書函得表一紙，始立表草，字皆難識，唯前有數行，稍可分辯，云：『天下之事，有善有惡，任善人則國安，用惡人則國亂。

translations.literal: After Zheng's death the emperor sent a man to his house; from his document case he obtained one memorial — the first draft of a memorial, the characters all hard to read; only the first several lines could be slightly distinguished, saying, 'Affairs under Heaven have good and evil; employ good men and the state is secure, employ evil men and the state is disordered.
translations.idiomatic: After Zheng's death the emperor sent a man to his house; from his papers came one memorial — a first draft, barely legible — whose opening lines read, 'Affairs under Heaven have good and evil; employ good men and the state is secure, employ evil men and the state is disordered.'

sentences.zh: 公卿之內，情有愛憎，憎者唯見其惡，愛者唯見其善。

translations.literal: Among the high ministers feelings of love and hate exist; those who hate see only their evil, those who love see only their good.
translations.idiomatic: Among high ministers love and hate exist; haters see only evil, lovers see only good.

sentences.zh: 愛憎之間，所宜詳慎，若愛而知其惡，憎而知其善，去邪勿疑，任賢勿貳，可以興矣。』

translations.literal: Between love and hate one must be detailed and careful; if one loves yet knows their evil, hates yet knows their good, removes the wicked without doubt and employs the worthy without division, the state can flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Between love and hate be careful; love yet know a man's faults, hate yet know his virtues, remove the wicked without doubt and employ the worthy without hesitation, and the state can flourish.

sentences.zh: 其遺表如此，然在朕思之，恐不免斯事。

translations.literal: His final memorial was thus — yet as I think on it, I fear I cannot avoid this matter.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial was thus — yet I fear I cannot avoid this failing.

sentences.zh: 公卿侍臣，可書之於笏，知而必諫也。」

translations.literal: High ministers and attending officials — write it on your tablets and knowing it, you must remonstrate."
translations.idiomatic: High ministers and attendants — write it on your tablets and remonstrate when you must."

sentences.zh: 徵狀貌不逾中人，而素有膽智，毎犯顏進諫，雖逢王赫斯怒，神色不移。

translations.literal: Zheng's appearance did not exceed a middling man, yet he was by nature possessed of courage and wisdom; whenever he corrected the countenance and advanced remonstrance, even meeting the king's sudden rage his expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng looked no more than average, yet he was bold and wise; when he remonstrated to the emperor's face, even under sudden rage his expression did not change.

sentences.zh: 嘗密薦中書侍郎杜正倫及吏部尚書侯君集有宰相之材。

translations.literal: He once secretly recommended Vice Director of the Secretariat Du Zhenglun and Minister of Personnel Hou Junji as possessed of chancellor's talent.
translations.idiomatic: He once secretly recommended Du Zhenglun, vice director of the Secretariat, and Hou Junji, minister of personnel, as chancellor material.

sentences.zh: 徵卒後，正倫以罪黜，君集犯逆伏誅，太宗始疑徵阿黨。

translations.literal: After Zheng's death, Zhenglun was dismissed for offense and Junji was executed for rebellion; Taizong then began to suspect Zheng of faction.
translations.idiomatic: After Zheng's death Zhenglun was dismissed for offense and Junji executed for rebellion; Taizong then suspected Zheng of faction.

sentences.zh: 徵又自録前後諫諍言辭往復以示史官起居郎褚遂良，太宗知之，愈不悅。

translations.literal: Zheng also himself recorded his former remonstrances and replies back and forth and showed them to the Diarist Attendant Chu Suiliang; when Taizong learned of it he was still less pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had also recorded his remonstrances and replies and showed them to diarist Chu Suiliang; Taizong, learning this, was still less pleased.

sentences.zh: 先許以衡山公主降其長子叔玉，於是手詔停婚，顧其家漸衰矣。

translations.literal: He had earlier promised to marry Princess Hengshan to his eldest son Shuyu; he therefore wrote an edict in his own hand stopping the marriage, and Zheng's house gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Having promised Princess Hengshan to his eldest son Shuyu, he now wrote an edict stopping the marriage, and Zheng's house gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 徵四子，叔琬、叔璘、叔瑜。

translations.literal: Zheng had four sons: Shuwan, Shulin, and Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had four sons — Shuwan, Shulin, and Shuyu — besides the heir Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 叔玉襲爵國公，官至光祿少卿；

translations.literal: Shuyu inherited the ducal fief and reached Vice Director of the Palace Library;
translations.idiomatic: Shuyu the heir inherited the ducal title and rose to vice director of the Palace Library;

sentences.zh: 叔瑜至潞州刺史，叔璘禮部侍郎，則天時爲酷吏所殺。

translations.literal: Shuyu reached Prefect of Lu, Shulin reached Vice Minister of Rites, and under Empress Wu was killed by cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyu became prefect of Lu; Shulin became vice minister of rites and under Empress Wu was killed by cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，繼封叔玉子膺爲鄭國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Shuyu's son Ying was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong, Shuyu's son Ying was enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng in succession.

sentences.zh: 叔瑜子華，開元初太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Shuyu's son Hua, at the beginning of Kaiyuan was Right Vice Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyu's son Hua was right vice mentor of the crown prince at the start of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：臣嘗讀漢史《劉更生傳》，見其上書論王氏擅權，恐移運祚，漢成不悟，更生徘徊伊郁，極言而不顧禍患，何匡益忠盡也如此！

translations.literal: The historian says: Your subject once read in the Han History the biography of Liu Gengsheng and saw him submit a memorial discussing the Wang clan's usurpation of power, fearing the transfer of the Mandate; Emperor Cheng did not understand, and Gengsheng wandered in distress, speaking to the utmost without regard for calamity — how loyal and exhaustive in benefiting the state was his correction!
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: I once read the Han History biography of Liu Gengsheng, who memorialized against Wang Mang's usurpation while Emperor Cheng failed to understand; Gengsheng wandered in distress and spoke without regard for peril — how loyal and thorough his service was!

sentences.zh: 當更生時，諫者甚多。

translations.literal: In Gengsheng's time, remonstrators were many.
translations.idiomatic: In Gengsheng's day remonstrators were many.

sentences.zh: 如谷永、楊興之上言，圖爲奸利，與賊臣爲鄕導，梅福、王吉之言，雖近古道，未切事情。

translations.literal: Such as Gu Yong and Yang Xing's upper memorials, plotting wicked profit and acting as guides for treacherous ministers; Mei Fu and Wang Ji's words, though near the ancient Way, did not cut to the heart of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong and Yang Xing plotted profit and guided traitors; Mei Fu and Wang Ji spoke in an antique vein but missed the point.

sentences.zh: 則納諫任賢，詎宜容易！

translations.literal: Then to accept remonstrance and employ the worthy — how can it be easy!
translations.idiomatic: To accept remonstrance and employ the worthy is no easy thing!

sentences.zh: 臣嘗閱《魏公故事》，與文皇討論政術，往復應對，凡數十萬言。

translations.literal: Your subject once read the Record of Duke Wei's deeds and saw him with Emperor Wen discuss methods of government, answering back and forth — in all several hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the Record of Duke Wei and his discussions with Emperor Taizong on government — several hundred thousand words in all.

sentences.zh: 其匡過弼違，能近取譬，博約連類，皆前代諍臣之不至者。

translations.literal: In correcting faults and supporting what was wrong, drawing near comparisons, broadly concise and linking categories — all are what remonstrating ministers of former ages did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: In correcting faults, drawing apt comparisons, and linking categories, he surpassed remonstrators of former ages.

sentences.zh: 其實根於道義，發爲律度，身正而心勁，上不負時主，下不阿權幸，中不侈親族，外不爲朋黨，不以逢時改節，不以圖位賣忠。

translations.literal: In truth rooted in righteousness and principle, issuing as law and measure, upright in person and firm in heart — above not failing the lord of the time, below not flattering the powerful and favored, in the middle not enlarging kin, outwardly not forming factions, not changing integrity to suit the times, not selling loyalty for position.
translations.idiomatic: Rooted in righteousness, issuing as law, upright in person and firm in heart — he failed no lord above, flattered no favorite below, enlarged no kin, formed no faction, changed no integrity for the times, and sold no loyalty for office.

sentences.zh: 所載章疎四篇，可爲萬代王者法。

translations.literal: The four memorials preserved can serve as law for myriade generations of kings.
translations.idiomatic: His four preserved memorials can serve as law for kings of ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 雖漢之劉向、魏之徐邈、晉之山濤、宋之謝朏，才則才矣，比文貞之雅道，不有遺行乎？

translations.literal: Though Han's Liu Xiang, Wei's Xu Miao, Jin's Shan Tao, and Song's Xie Tiao had talent — compared with Wenzhen's upright Way, do they not leave conduct unrecorded?
translations.idiomatic: Han's Liu Xiang, Wei's Xu Miao, Jin's Shan Tao, and Song's Xie Tiao had talent — yet beside Wenzhen's upright Way, do they not leave conduct wanting?

sentences.zh: 前代諍臣，一人而已。

translations.literal: Among remonstrating ministers of former ages, there is only one man.
translations.idiomatic: Among remonstrating ministers of former ages, there is only one such man.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：智者不諫，諫或不智。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The wise do not remonstrate; those who remonstrate may not be wise.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The wise do not remonstrate; remonstrators may not be wise.

sentences.zh: 智者盡言，國家之利。

translations.literal: When the wise speak to the full, it is the state's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When the wise speak fully, the state benefits.

sentences.zh: 鄭公達節，才周經濟。

translations.literal: Duke Zheng reached integrity; his talent encompassed statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zheng reached integrity; his talent encompassed statecraft.

sentences.zh: 太宗用之，子孫長世。

translations.literal: Taizong employed him; his descendants lasted generations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong employed him; his line lasted generations.
